title: Trying game dev with ai for the first time with VSCode - ?
author: sir_daviid
selftext:
I am going to try to do some vibe coding for the first time using VSCode, however after installing, I can't seem to find a way to purely vibe code without any coding experience. The copilot tells me  
"For making a 2D game without writing code, try GDevelop. It has a visual event system and is a good fit for a top-down maze game. It’s a separate app, not a VS Code extension, and you don’t need the JDK or VS Code to use it."  
So what should I try instead?  Hopefully this makes sense.

comments.author: novashiftinteractVN
comments.body: If you want a Text editor with AI as I remember Cursor it's a good option. anyway the most common way to vibe coding right now it's using the cli's like Claude Code, Codex, Opencode etc

comments.author: Hallucinates_Bacon
comments.body: Claude code. Pull up vs code when you need to read files

replies.author: Own_Badger6076
replies.body: I mean they could also install the CC extension in vscode and just run it through there as well.

comments.author: imlo2
comments.body: Do you have a paid Claude or ChatGPT account? If you do, then you can use Claude Code or Codex. But the first thing you do is ask from a proper LLM for steps.

comments.author: Sith_Lord_Aries
comments.body:
If you are trying to go local only, you ether need great hardware or you already have to kinda know what you are doing.

Newer models work the best so try for the latest you can fit.  I had good luck with Bonsai models as they are small enough to fit better.

Cloud based vibe coding is the current meta however.  Ive a buddy useing Claude and I picked up googles Antigravity and we are passing the game back and forth between us.

The only thing that local ai beats the cloud ai is in image generation.  No limits in the stuff I make on my system.  Useing the image generator from Antigravity only gave me like 15 images every 5 hours!  Luckily it can hook into my local image generator (comfyUi) and no longer be my bottle neck.

comments.author: PlantLegacyGame
comments.body: I'm using the kilo code extension for free and using the nvidia nemotron 3 ultra model and the opencode app (I think they harvest your data to give free ai lol), probably better free stuff out there but just use kilo code if you want a freebie since you already got vs code installed.

comments.author: sir_daviid
comments.body: So when it says select type of build tools, what should I pick?

replies.author: Vindelator
replies.body:
Try this: Google search claude or claude. Say "i want to make my first game using html and javascript. Tell me the steps to make it starting from the basics in simple language."

Pick a type of game that was around in the 90s and make your version of it.

Get a $20 monthly claude sub. The knowledge you'll pick up is worth far more than 20 bucks.

replies.author: dvorgson
replies.body: this guy's not asking how to write code. he's asking how to jump into vibe coding

replies.author: Vindelator
replies.body: I know. That's what I told him. Claude will write stuff if give it that setup

comments.author: semantic_miasis
comments.body: Recomendación. 1- aprende lo mínimo de programación y el motor que usas (3 meses maximo), 2- usa algo llamado SDD para programar con IA, el vibe coding es una receta para el desastre
